title: Every enemy once
prompt:
`enemies.txt` lists the enemies the play-testers met, one per line, with many repeats. Save a sorted list with every name only once into `enemies-sorted.txt`.

Names that differ in case, such as `Skeleton` and `skeleton`, count as different names.
hints: `sort` sorts lines. `uniq` drops a line that repeats the line right before it, which is why it usually comes after `sort`.
`sort enemies.txt | uniq` prints each name once. `sort -u` does both in one step.
check:
if [ ! -e enemies-sorted.txt ]; then no "There is no enemies-sorted.txt yet. Create it in Mira’s home directory."; exit 1; fi
ok "enemies-sorted.txt exists."
if [ "$(cat enemies-sorted.txt)" = "$(sort -u enemies.txt)" ]; then ok "It holds every enemy once, sorted."
elif [ "$(sort enemies-sorted.txt)" = "$(sort -u enemies.txt)" ]; then no "It has every name once, but not sorted."
else no "It doesn’t hold each name of enemies.txt exactly once. Compare it with sort enemies.txt."; fi
if [ "$(wc -l < enemies.txt)" = 11 ]; then ok "enemies.txt itself is unchanged."; else no "enemies.txt changed. Write the result to a new file."; fi

title: What went wrong in the build?
prompt:
Ada’s nightly build wrote `build.log`. Mira wants two files for the stand-up meeting:

1. `errors.txt`: every line of `build.log` that contains `ERROR`, in the original order.
2. `error-count.txt`: just the number of those lines.
hints: `grep ERROR build.log` prints the matching lines.
`grep -c` counts matching lines instead of printing them; `wc -l` counts the lines it reads.
`grep ERROR build.log > errors.txt` and `grep -c ERROR build.log > error-count.txt`.
solution:
grep ERROR build.log > errors.txt
grep -c ERROR build.log > error-count.txt
check:
if [ ! -e errors.txt ]; then no "There is no errors.txt yet. Create it in Mira’s home directory."; exit 1; fi
ok "errors.txt exists."
if [ "$(cat errors.txt)" = "$(grep ERROR build.log)" ]; then ok "errors.txt holds exactly the ERROR lines."
else no "errors.txt doesn’t hold exactly the lines of build.log that contain ERROR."; fi
if [ ! -e error-count.txt ]; then no "There is no error-count.txt yet. Create it in Mira’s home directory."; exit 1; fi
ok "error-count.txt exists."
if [ "$(tr -d ' \n' < error-count.txt)" = "$(grep -c ERROR build.log)" ]; then ok "error-count.txt holds the right number."
else no "error-count.txt holds “$(head -c 40 error-count.txt)”, which isn’t the number of ERROR lines."; fi

title: Output here, errors there
prompt:
Jonas’s checklist script runs `ls art music` to list two folders, but `music` doesn’t exist yet, so `ls` complains.

Run that same command once, so that the normal listing goes into `listing.txt` and the error message goes into `errors.txt`. Neither file may hold the other one’s text.
hints: Programs write normal output to standard output (stream 1) and error messages to standard error (stream 2).
`>` redirects stream 1; `2>` redirects stream 2. One command can have both.
check:
if [ ! -e listing.txt ]; then no "There is no listing.txt yet. Create it in Mira’s home directory."; exit 1; fi
ok "listing.txt exists."
if [ ! -e errors.txt ]; then no "There is no errors.txt yet. Create it in Mira’s home directory."; exit 1; fi
ok "errors.txt exists."
if grep -q 'hero.png' listing.txt && ! grep -q 'No such file' listing.txt; then ok "listing.txt holds the listing of art and no error."
else no "listing.txt should hold the listing of art (hero.png …) and no error message."; fi
if grep -q "music.*No such file" errors.txt && ! grep -q 'hero.png' errors.txt; then ok "errors.txt holds the error about music, and nothing else."
else no "errors.txt should hold only the error message about music."; fi
